POLO 2.4.7 — Sessions & System Refresh V2

## NEW

- Sessions V2 now runs through a persistent native state machine with pre-flight review, duplicate-session locking, WAITING / ACTIVE / PAUSED / RECOVERABLE states, a crash-safe journal and versioned local reports.
- Session process detection uses explicit executable mappings where available. Missing frame data remains NOT MEASURED; POLO never invents FPS, game ping or comparison results.
- Closing POLO completely opens an optional local 1–10 feedback screen that can be disabled or restored from Settings.

## IMPROVED

- RAM Lab groups multi-process apps and separates PROTECTED, MANUAL, ELIGIBLE and evidence-backed RECOMMENDED states.
- RAM actions use an immutable 60-second backend plan and revalidate PID, creation time, executable path, Windows session and protection rules immediately before trimming.
- Results now say “immediate working-set reduction” instead of “RAM reclaimed,” and separately report executed, skipped and measured outcomes.
- Storage Lab builds a five-minute immutable candidate plan, revalidates every file before deletion and rescans the selected fixed roots afterward.
- Storage hides empty categories by default, leaves shader caches unselected and clearly separates LAST VERIFIED CLEANUP from CURRENT SCAN.
- Top CPU processes show real Windows executable icons when available, with a generic fallback.

## FIXED

- Existing POLO Community usernames now guide members directly to Sign in without carrying the registration-only error into the login form.
- Passwords shorter than 12 characters show a clear requirement and disabled action state.
- A successful registration no longer appears to fail when Windows secure session storage is temporarily unavailable.

## SECURITY & PRIVACY

- Storage cleanup receives only a backend-issued plan ID; raw frontend paths are never deletion authority.
- Reparse points, stale or changed files, out-of-root paths, protected processes and expired plans are skipped or rejected.
- RAM and Storage mutations share one lock and cannot run simultaneously.
- Session journals, System Refresh Evidence, process icons and exit feedback remain local.
- POLO Community still prefers Windows DPAPI-backed token storage; the emergency fallback is session-only.

Password recovery is not available in this release. Existing members must sign in with their original password.
